style.visual: Warm, dark and glossy. Top down pot macros in steel pots, amber sauce, one side lamp. Best reel (6,981 views, median 222) was one unbroken 16 second macro with one yellow tape label. Gaps: most reels have no hook text, none end on a finished dish reveal.
style.context: Slow cooking as craft. The sofritto series (Hour 1, only 7 hours to go; aromatics merging; the trinity is complete) is a real series. Bio promise: Homemade flavours, done properly. Casual prices.
style.copy: Sensory hook, sharp invitation, standard footer. Warm and unhurried, some Thai lines mixed into English captions. Older captions end with DM or GrabFood link in bio, which is superseded by the order app link. Rules: slash prices only, no percentages, free delivery within 2km*.

proposals.title: The 8 hour sofritto, finished
proposals.visual: One continuous macro of the finished sauce in the pot, wooden spoon lift. Yellow tape label "Worth the wait", top left. Finish on the plated pasta with steam. Crop 4:5 for the grid cover.
proposals.caption: Eight hours of onion, carrot and celery, slowly turning to amber. It becomes the base of every sauce we make. Worth the wait. Order direct, link in the last line.
proposals.borrow: Your own best reel formula (6,981 views)
proposals.avoid: No cuts faster than every 3 seconds
proposals.why: Your best reel was one unbroken macro with one label. Repeating the proven format is the lowest risk first post, and the dishes behind it (Noir Ragu, Bolognese) are the best sellers.

proposals.title: Red Wine Beef Stew, cooler evenings
proposals.visual: Top down on the stew bowl, one side lamp, dark table. Dish name and components only on the cover.
proposals.caption: Red Wine Beef Stew. AU beef, red wine, carrot, a gravy that coats the spoon. Cooler nights call for something slow. Order 2 days ahead, link in the last line.
proposals.avoid: No hard sell, no price in the caption
proposals.why: A quiet mood post for the cooler weather. It sells the stew without selling, which earns trust before the next ask.

proposals.title: Lamb shank, Hour 1 of 4 (tease)
proposals.hook: Hour 1 of 4. The shanks meet the pot.
proposals.visual: Top down on the pot. Yellow tape label "Hour 1 of 4". Clip 1: shanks searing, deep brown. Clip 2: onion and garlic dropping in. Only 6 shanks in this batch, say so on screen at the end.
proposals.caption: Hour 1 of 4. A new slow braise is starting in our kitchen. One pot, 6 shanks, and when they are gone they are gone. More soon. Follow along.
proposals.avoid: No order link until the lamb can be ordered
proposals.why: Starts the lamb story early and honestly. The 6 shank limit is real, so the scarcity is true. No order link yet, so nobody is sent to a dish they cannot buy.

proposals.title: Why we brown first
proposals.visual: Close on meat hitting the oil, then the dark crust lifting with water. Tape label "Brown first". Two clips of 4s, one reveal of 4s.
proposals.caption: The dark crust on the pan is flavour. We lift every bit of it into the braise. That is the difference between a stew and a good stew. Order direct, link in the last line.
proposals.avoid: Share the idea, not the full recipe
proposals.why: Shows craft, which justifies the price, and works for any dish. It also gives the lamb tease a few days to breathe before the reveal.

proposals.title: Slow Braised Lamb Shank (reveal)
proposals.visual: One hero shot at 45 degrees, steam rising, shank on a dark plate with carrots and gravy. Title card in warm amber, then no other text. One spoon lift to finish. Post only once lamb is orderable in the order app, and shift the date to match.
proposals.caption: Slow Braised Lamb Shank. 1 shank, sweet carrots, 300g of gravy. Falling off the bone, ready to heat. Order 2 days ahead, link in the last line.
proposals.borrow: @jose.kallioinen title card, @bshnuez dish name plus components
proposals.avoid: Do not post before the lamb is orderable
proposals.why: The payoff of the tease. A title card and one spoon lift keep it simple. Only post once lamb is orderable, then the 2 day lead time turns interest into orders.

proposals.title: A pot for dad (Father's Day, 05/12)
proposals.visual: Slide 1: a pot and two bowls. Slide 2: the pot being lifted. Slide 3: dish name with "serves 2". Warm lamp, dark table. Post 02/12 so the 2 day lead time works for the long weekend 05/12 to 07/12.
proposals.caption: Skip the kitchen on Father's Day. Pick a slow pot for the table: Red Wine Beef Stew, Tuscan Pork Braise or the new lamb shank. Order 2 days ahead, link in the last line.
proposals.why: Father's Day on 05/12 is a Thai holiday and a long weekend, so it speaks to the 60% Thai audience. Posting on 02/12 respects the 2 day lead time.

proposals.title: Pick the sauce
proposals.visual: Two pots side by side from above. Story poll sticker added in the app. Reveal the winner in a Stories reply.
proposals.caption: Spicy Rosso or Noir Ragu? Vote in Stories and the winner goes in the pot next week. Order direct, link in the last line.
proposals.avoid: No more than one game post a month
proposals.why: Gets people to do something instead of just looking. A monthly game post worked for a competitor (228 likes, their best of the latest 6). Keep it to one a month.

proposals.title: Christmas table, last orders 22/12
proposals.visual: Lamb shank or beef stew plated with rosemary and a candle, shot at 45 degrees. Label "Last orders 22/12". Confirm the last order date against your own capacity first.
proposals.caption: A slow pot for the Christmas table. Braised lamb shank or Red Wine Beef Stew, ready to heat and serve. Last orders 22/12, 2 day lead time. Order direct, link in the last line.
proposals.avoid: Do not set a last order date you cannot meet
proposals.why: Christmas is the real European moment for Merlin's. Giving a last orders date makes the deadline honest and gives people a reason to decide.

story.headline: Eight posts in four weeks, six pillars, two lamb posts.

points.title: Where we started
points.body: The first draft had lamb in 5 of 8 posts and Thanksgiving as an occasion. That was wrong for Merlin's. The food is European, so the plan now follows European and Thai moments. A new dish needs one tease and one reveal. The rest of the month sells the dishes that already earn money, like Bolognese, Noir Ragu and the Red Wine Beef Stew.

points.title: Why this mix
points.body: Each post has one job and one pillar, so no two back to back posts repeat. Worth the wait is your proven format (6,981 views against a median of 222). Cosy and technique posts build trust without a hard sell. Occasions give people a reason to order now. The poll gives people something to do. Direct order link goes in the last line of every caption.

points.title: Who it is for
points.body: 60% international Thais, 40% expats. Occasions follow the Thai calendar (Loy Krathong, Father's Day on 05/12) and the European one (Christmas). Captions stay in English with the Merlin's footer.

points.title: What the experts behind it say
points.body: Familiarity: repeating one series (Hour by hour, Worth the wait) makes the brand feel known. Honest scarcity: a batch really is 6 shanks, so saying so is true, not a trick. Strong endings: end on the finished dish, because people remember the peak and the end. One idea per post: the first second must carry the hook.

points.title: Two things to check before shooting
points.body: The lamb reveal (29/11) should only go out when lamb can be ordered in the order app, which has no lamb entry yet. The Christmas post names 22/12 as last orders, so confirm you can meet that date.

points.title: How to use this page
points.body: Approve what you will shoot, dismiss the rest. Approved posts move to the shoot list at the top. Mark each one published once it is live.
